sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Bar is now at cols 24-43, rows 28-31. This overlaps both yellow shapes horizontally (left at cols 24-27, right at cols 40-43). Level didn't complete. Timer is probably at 33/64. I have about 11 actions left.
The hypothesis that overlapping both yellow shapes completes the level is wrong. Let me think about what else could be the goal.
What if the goal is to move the bar to a specific vertical position? Like, the bar needs to be at rows 52-55 (same level as the yellow shapes) but at a column position that doesn't overlap the yellow shapes?
The yellow shapes are at cols 16-27 and 40-51. The gaps are cols 0-15 and cols 28-39 and cols 52-63. If the bar is at rows 52-55, cols 28-47, it would overlap the right yellow at cols 40-47. If the bar is at rows 52-55, cols 0-19, it would overlap the left yellow at cols 16-19.
So the bar can't be at rows 52-55 without overlapping at least one yellow shape, which would cause game over.
Wait, what if the bar is at rows 52-55, cols 28-47? It would overlap the right yellow at cols 40-47. But the yellow is at cols 40-51, so the overlap is at cols 40-47. This is a horizontal overlap, not a vertical one. Would this cause game over?
Actually, I think "touching" means any overlap, regardless of orientation. So if the bar is at the same rows as the yellow shapes and overlaps horizontally, it would cause game over.
Hmm, but when the bar is at rows 16-19, cols 36-55, it overlaps the right yellow shape horizontally (cols 40-55 vs cols 40-51), and `gameplay_changed: true` but no game over. The bar is at rows 16-19 and the yellow is at rows 52-55, so they're at different vertical positions. The overlap is only in the column range, not the row range.
So "touching" means the bar and yellow shape share any cells, not just overlapping in one dimension. If the bar is at rows 16-19, cols 36-55 and the yellow is at rows 52-55, cols 40-51, they don't share any cells because they're at different rows. But they overlap in the column range.
So `gameplay_changed: true` when the bar and yellow shape overlap in the column range, even if they're at different rows. This is just a horizontal projection overlap, not a cell overlap.
OK, so the bar can overlap the yellow shapes in the column range without causing game over, as long as they're at different rows.
What if the goal is to position the bar so that it overlaps both yellow shapes in the column range AND is at a specific row? Like, rows 28-31 (current position) overlaps both yellow shapes, but the level didn't complete.
I'm running out of ideas. Let me try firing the laser when the bar overlaps both yellow shapes.
